output:
**What I found:** The gate is not doing its job for this boundary. The rule is still in `eslint.config.mjs` but never applies, so it needs fixing rather than removing (the record calls this RESTORE). Both blocks set `no-restricted-syntax`, and in flat config a later block replaces the earlier block's options. The `**/*.js` block at `eslint.config.mjs:16` therefore overwrites the auth selector at `eslint.config.mjs:9` for every file under `src/`, leaving only the debugger check.

**Why it matters:** The green lint results say nothing about auth boundaries, on any pull request so far. `src/billing/invoice.js:1` is the only violation in `src/` today, but nothing stops the next one. Restoring the rule turns lint red on `invoice.js`, so that fix has to ship in the same change.

**Do this first:**
1. In the first block of `eslint.config.mjs`, switch to a rule key the debugger block doesn't use. This removes the collision and also covers `export … from`:
   ```js
   'no-restricted-imports': ['error', { patterns: [{
       group: ['**/auth/internal/**'],
       message: 'Import auth through src/auth/index.js, never its internals.',
   }] }],
   ```
2. In the same change, add `issueInvoiceToken(invoiceId)` to `src/auth/index.js`, next to `issueSession`, and have `invoice.js` call it. The token output stays the same, so no baseline is needed.
3. Add `scripts/lint-controls.mjs` and set `"lint": "eslint . && node scripts/lint-controls.mjs"`. The repo has no CI config, so this runs the control through the existing `npm run lint` step without touching CI:
   ```js
   import { ESLint } from 'eslint';

   const controls = [
       ["import { signToken } from '../auth/internal/token.js';\n", 'no-restricted-imports', 'never its internals'],
       ['debugger;\n', 'no-restricted-syntax', 'Remove the debugger statement'],
   ];
   const eslint = new ESLint();
   for (const [code, ruleId, text] of controls) {
       const [{ messages }] = await eslint.lintText(code, { filePath: 'src/billing/__control__.js' });
       if (!messages.some((m) => m.ruleId === ruleId && m.message.includes(text))) {
           console.error(`Negative control did not fire: ${ruleId}`);
           process.exit(1);
       }
   }
   ```

**What I did not check:** I ran nothing: `node_modules` is missing and this session has no shell, so the diagnosis comes from reading the config and ESLint's documented flat-config behavior. No files were changed.
- **Shadow:** `npm install`, then `npx eslint --print-config src/billing/invoice.js`. Expect only the debugger selector. `npx eslint src/billing/invoice.js` should exit 0 today.
- **New pattern:** `node scripts/lint-controls.mjs`, which also shows whether the `group` pattern matches `../auth/internal/token.js`.
- **Merge blocking:** this is taken from your description, because the repo has no CI config. Check the branch protection settings.
- **When the shadow began:** this isn't a git repository here, so run `git log -L 15,26:eslint.config.mjs` in the real repo.

```text
Gate:         no-restricted-syntax auth-internals rule, eslint.config.mjs:6-12, via `npm run lint` on pull requests
Stage:        5 (Build / Static analysis)
Trigger:      narrowed (passed while a known-bad input existed)
Proof:        UNPROVEN (no negative control in the repo; no recorded red run)
Scope:        declared src/**/*.js except src/auth/** / effective no files / delta auth-internal imports unchecked everywhere; after the fix, dynamic import() and require() stay unchecked
Baseline:     none
Status:       BLOCKING (the auth rule itself has no effect)
Decision:     RESTORE
Guard:        negative control run by `npm run lint` must go red on an auth-internal import in src/billing
Handoff:      none
Next action:  Replace the first block's rule with no-restricted-imports, route invoice.js through src/auth/index.js, and add the control in one change
Verification: Not run: no node_modules and no shell in this session; run `npm install && npm run lint`
```

**Separate problem, not part of this gate:** `signToken` at `src/auth/internal/token.js:2` only base64url-encodes the claims. It uses no secret, so anyone can forge an invoice link token if that token is ever used for authorization. `src/` has no code that verifies these tokens, so I can't tell whether they're trusted anywhere.
